account:
Today the unusual thing has been the gap between ordinary business and the rumours growing around it. At tea, my neighbour said they personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery. They also said Townsfolk 02 reported bridge changes and decorating, but provided no firsthand details when asked. The neighbour heard no announcement of changes, and said the baker knew of no celebration. I have not witnessed those supposed changes or decorations myself. My best guess is that delivery questions have become embellished as people repeat them; I cannot yet establish anyone's intention beyond the apparent collection and delivery business.

The builder reported no confirmed damage at the bridge, ferry, or warehouse. There was an inspection proposal, but I authorized neither paid inspections nor repairs. I have also authorized no bridge or port changes and have no confirmed celebration to announce. These are separate from any rumours people may be circulating.

For town accounts, I personally checked the treasury and saw 128 emeralds in two stacks, with no ledger present. I removed nothing. That establishes the contents I saw, not verified income or expenses. The secretary says the accounts minutes and balance addendum are filed in the office chest, recording my no-spending decision and the balance qualification. No new correspondence or meeting requests had reached the secretary this afternoon.

I kept my afternoon office and tea appointments and am now home for the seven o'clock appointment. Tomorrow's ten o'clock mill visit is a routine grain inspection; I asked the secretary to request stock and delivery records, without authorizing spending. Tomorrow's three o'clock tea is confirmed at the same east-bank cottage. I should read my appointment book in the morning and keep the rest of the day's schedule.
